sn22.90:3.11: All conditions are impermanent, all things are not-self’.
sn22.90:5.1: “Once, Reverend Ānanda, at one time I was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.
sn22.90:5.2: Then, friend, in the late afternoon I came out of retreat. Taking a latchkey, I went from dwelling to dwelling;
sn22.90:5.3: going up to the senior mendicants, I said:
sn22.90:5.4: ‘May the venerable senior mendicants advise me and instruct me! May they give me a Dhamma talk so that I can see the teaching’.
sn22.90:5.5: When I had said this, friend, the senior mendicants said:
sn22.90:5.13: All conditions are impermanent, all things are not-self’.
sn22.90:6.1: Then, friend, this occurred to me:
sn22.90:6.4: and consciousness are impermanent, form is not-self, feeling …
sn22.90:6.8: All conditions are impermanent, all things are not-self’.
sn22.90:6.9: And yet my mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided about the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.
sn22.90:6.11: and keeps turning back to the thought:
sn22.90:6.13: But that doesn’t happen for someone who sees the teaching.
sn22.90:6.14: Who can teach me the Dhamma so that I can see the teaching?
sn22.90:7.1: Then, friend, this occurred to me:
sn22.90:7.2: ‘Venerable Ānanda is staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery. He’s praised by the Buddha and esteemed by his sensible spiritual companions. He’s quite capable of teaching me the Dhamma so that I can see the teaching.
sn22.90:7.3: Since I have so much trust in Venerable Ānanda,
sn22.90:7.4: why don’t I go to see him’?
sn22.90:7.6: May he instruct me, Venerable Ānanda;
sn22.90:7.7: May he give me, Venerable Ānanda, a Dhamma talk so that I can see the teaching”.
